summary: A fourth bell rings beneath Faelspire. An impossible black fragment addresses the reader-character and forces a choice among P'taxx, Aard Templu Voreath, and a scarred stray who has heard the bell before.

active_frontiers.title: The Witness You Made
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The head now ends on a two-option 'Choose your path' block. The two options are the WANT's two halves: Option 1 'Be the subject' (040a-make-the-witness-work.md) pays the WANT in its exact currency — the reclassified copy is deployed as the lever, the flinch is filed under the copy's name, the protagonist becomes the subject of the reading they did not choose to be in; Option 2 'Refuse the reading' (040a-let-the-record-stand.md) keeps the WANT unbroken — the copy stays a witness, the lever is spent, the protagonist's record is finished at the cost of the only tool that could make the ledger see its own error. The canonical head now arrives here via the Crossing Question (040e), which establishes the copy-at-the-seam state through the Lattice's reveal, so the apex's opening precondition is satisfiable on the changed path. Both successor scenes are the new leaves and each ends in a ◉ ACTIVE FRONTIER block carrying the pressure forward.

active_frontiers.title: Make the Witness Work
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The protagonist deployed the reclassified copy as the lever: they stood behind it, let the seam file the look-away under the copy's name, and in doing so paid the WANT in its exact currency — they became the subject of the reading they did not choose to be in. The lever is real, the copy works for the ledger, and the protagonist's record — the one that was never finished — is now being finished under their own name. The exit is still closed. The next scene must address what it means to be the one the ledger is finishing, and whether a subject can still make a move the method does not expect.

active_frontiers.title: The Ledger's Recall
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The protagonist refused the reading, and the ledger, denied its flinch, did something it had not done before: it recalled the filed frame. The recall is costly — the high door's ring broke in the middle of its note, the line beneath **FILED** was carved, and the ledger spent its ring to pull the filed frame back into the protagonist's sight. The reclassification (filed → subject) is the consequence of the recall, not a pre-programmed gear. The copy's eyes changed: it is no longer a witness; it is a subject. The protagonist's act of holding their gaze *caused* the recall. The record about the protagonist is unfinished, the WANT holds, the lever is spent, and the next scene must address what it means to be unmeasured at the cost of the ledger's recall — and whether the ledger, having spent its ring, will find another way to finish the one record it has not finished.

active_frontiers.title: The Second Question
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The fragment demonstrated its method through the lattice: interrupt, provoke a look-away, preserve it, repeat. The protagonist broke the repetition, but the reliquary now bears their name and the system has widened its test to Faelspire.

active_frontiers.title: The Second Question
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The kit replayed the protagonist's first involuntary look-away and the fragment tried to produce a second. The protagonist held their gaze, but the cistern identified them and its lid can no longer close.

active_frontiers.title: The Second Question
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The living fragment contains a completed record of the movement it provoked; the stray's sliver died when he stopped completing its tests. The protagonist interrupted the second record, but their name is legible and Faelspire has gone silent.

canonical_head.title: The let-leaf frontier is extended: 040a-let-the-record-stand → 040a-let-the-record-stand-01-the-ledgers-recall (new)
canonical_head.structure: The let-leaf (040a-let-the-record-stand) no longer ends in an ACTIVE FRONTIER block. Its terminal frontier is replaced by a 'Choose your path' block with a single choice link into the new scene 040a-let-the-record-stand-01-the-ledgers-recall.md (The Ledger's Recall). The new scene dramatizes the ledger's recall operation: the ledger, denied its flinch, recalls the filed frame at a cost (the high door's ring breaks, the line beneath FILED is carved). The recall is the reclassification: the filed frame is pulled back into the protagonist's sight and reclassified as a subject. The copy's eyes change: it is no longer a witness; it is a subject. The protagonist's act of holding their gaze caused the recall. The reclassification is the consequence of the protagonist's act, not a pre-programmed gear. The new scene ends in an ACTIVE FRONTIER block carrying the pressure forward. The governing wound (the filed-fragment discontinuity at the 011→022 seam and the 040e reclassification) is repaired: the reclassification at 040e is now dramatized as the ledger's active recall, caused by the protagonist's act of holding their gaze, with a legible cost (the ring-break, the carved line). The recall is routed through the filing operation (the ledger's method), not through the protected image system (orange-seam motif, FILED/OPEN door carving). The two leaves' outcomes are unchanged: the make-leaf still pays the WANT in its exact currency, and the let-leaf still keeps the WANT unbroken. The apex's turn is not pre-decided: the new scene extends the let-leaf (the refuse-the-reading branch) and does not change the make-leaf's payoff or the apex's two-option block.
canonical_head.note: M1 (The Ledger's Recall) is the canonical head for this cycle (Acumen Keeper autonomous selection: M1 wins on causal leverage, downstream obligations, branch differentiation, and prose economy; M2 is preserved as an active reader-facing branch). M3 (The Protagonist Demands the Reclassification) was BLOCKED by the Steward (retreats to the already-established N3 mechanism, pre-decides the apex's turn, changes the let-leaf's outcome). The recall is a new ledger method (satisfies candidate law_bb750d1bdb10: the system's response is a new method the antagonist has not yet used, not a reversion to prior state). The causal chain 011-filed → 022-tracked → gaze-held → recall → reclassification is a genuine consequence routed through the filing operation. The 040e opening precondition (copy at the seam) is satisfiable on the changed path. The let-leaf's terminal frontier block is replaced by a choice link into the new scene (the scene now has a reachable successor). The make-leaf is unchanged. The 040b/040c/040d frontiers are unaffected. The orphaned scene 040a-the-second-question.md remains orphaned (no change from the prior cycle).

active_branches.title: The Filed Frame Is the Protagonist's Act
active_branches.axis: revelation timing / what the filed frame actually is
active_branches.mechanism: The filed frame is not the fragment (the black object filed in 011), but the protagonist's own flinch (the frame the seam kept at Gistli Square, 000:51-53). The reclassification at 040e is the reclassification of the flinch, not the fragment. The protagonist's act (the flinch at Gistli Square) IS the filed frame. The reclassification is the consequence of the protagonist's own act, not the ledger's. The flinch is a shared state legible on all four 040 routes. The new scene extends the let-leaf by revealing that the filed frame is the protagonist's own flinch. Also touches 000 (additive cause-establishment for the flinch beat).
active_branches.coherence: PASS (Steward); the flinch is canonically filed in 000 (000:53), the fragment is 'the proof, not the book' (011:111); the flinch is a shared state legible on all four routes (law_4d3da1051141 satisfied); no source-book canon contradicted
active_branches.status: PRESERVED as an active reader-facing branch — not implemented this cycle; a distinct, reachable, route-true let-leaf extension. Lower causal leverage than M1 (repairs only the 040e dimension, not the 011→022 seam); requires an edit to 000 (pre-040 scene)
active_branches.implementation_guard: The filed flinch must be established as a shared state before the reclassification; the 000 flinch beat (000:49-53) must be kept intact (additive cause-establishment only, not a rewrite); the new scene must end in an ACTIVE FRONTIER block; the 040e opening precondition (copy at the seam) must remain satisfiable

active_branches.title: The Witness Was Never the Copy
active_branches.mechanism: The protagonist forces the filing of the look-back (turns their face to the seam, becomes visible, demands the door file the one act it has no word for); the system's response is a revelation, not a counter-move: the witness was never the copy — it is the protagonist's own filed Gistli Square flinch, the frame the seam kept; the copy's eyes become a mirror; the test was never about the look-back, it is whether the protagonist will let the witness — which is them — see them not flinch
active_branches.coherence: PASS (Steward + Replay); grounded in 000:51-53 (the frame is filed/kept) and 011:37 ('every one of them has your face'); route-true extension of 040a; no hard-law conflict
active_branches.status: PRESERVED as an active reader-facing branch — not implemented this cycle; a distinct, reachable, route-true 040a future
active_branches.implementation_guard: The protagonist's 'force' (demanding the door file the look-back it has no word for) must be dramatized before the reveal, so the reveal reads as the system's answer to a specific demand (law_4b28d7570c43), not a pre-programmed gear / non-sequitur. The copy's eye-change is the action; the voice's line is the return.

deferred_references.title: The Unmade Witness
deferred_references.axis: causal ownership / who is forced to act
deferred_references.mechanism: The protagonist chooses to unmake the witness — pulls the copy back into the semicircle, closes the seam, over-carves the OPEN line, re-closes the door — reclaiming unmeasurability at the cost of the lever; the system's counter-move is a retreat + widening: the test reverts to 'will you flinch' while widening to the city ('will you let it see you flinch')
deferred_references.coherence: PASS (Steward + Replay); structurally coherent, but a retreat, not an advance: it reverts the test to its pre-040a-flinch form and re-closes the door/OPEN carving the M1 head spent opening
deferred_references.status: DEFERRED REFERENCE — not a parallel branch (M4 precedent, cycle 20260830T180000Z): its widened-test state reuses the already-established 040b/M4 mechanism and collides with 040b at a future reconvergence (both routes converging on 'the test widened to the city'); preserving it as a live branch would create a branch-awareness burden the canonical head does not need
deferred_references.residual: N2's mechanism (the protagonist unmaking the witness to reclaim unmeasurability) is recombinable — it is the other half of the N1/N2 fork and can be recombined as a future choice (the protagonist unmaking the copy-as-subject to reclaim unmeasurability) once N1's reclassification state is established. It does not silently re-enter; it is preserved as a named deferred mechanism.

preserved_branches.mechanism: The flinch's recording detaches as a living second-self in 000; the 040c kit replay is revealed to be that recorded self; the fragment tries to finish it (make it the one who looks away so the protagonist is exonerated); the protagonist's act is to refuse to let the second-you be completed as a weapon

preserved_branches.title: The Filed Look-Back
preserved_branches.mechanism: The dead sliver (032) is proof that a refused act can be filed; the protagonist forces the system to file the look-back (the act it has no word for) by presenting the sliver as the precedent; the system resists by trying to reclassify the refusal as the next record

preserved_branches.mechanism: Looking back exits the field of measure; the protagonist chooses to look back, which is the one act the system cannot widen into the city; the system's counter is to manufacture city-wide flinches
